system.biography:
Background

Formerly the Black Prince of Cornwall, Embraced in 1432 and betrayed by his own sire, Sir Lorence, who murdered Scott's mortal wife and son as part of the Embrace, Edward Scott fled to the New World and eventually settled in Milwaukee, where he now sits on the city's ruling Council as the self-appointed "Prince of the Anarchs." He deliberately courts scandal — attending Council meetings in a bathrobe or bikini — to bait the Elders and remind them of the vitality he believes their "soft and fat" ancient wisdom has lost. He sired the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.ZFYurbvAHfaRguYI]{Brujah} elder Akawa (whom he does not remember Embracing) and maintains an intense, decades-long friendly rivalry with him; the two have nearly killed each other in the dueling grounds on multiple occasions, always without a clear winner, and Scott has saved Akawa from a Blood Hunt more than once. Scott has significant, if informal, influence over both major Anarch gangs, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.antitribu.JournalEntry.hs33xrNXWT2UXXS4]{Blood Brothers} and the Union, and personally challenges any Elder (such as Gracis Nostinus) who threatens to move against the Anarchs over a Masquerade breach.

Roleplaying Hints

Smile constantly, mock everyone (Elders, Anarchs, mortals, and himself), never show real anger, and compliment every woman present regardless of context. Underneath the theatrical rebel is genuine centuries-old grief and rage at how Elders prey on the young and weak.
system.notes: Sire: Sir Lorence (who killed Scott's mortal family as part of the Embrace). Haven: a small, elegant apartment on Milwaukee's east side near the lake. Disciplines as printed: Auspex 1, Celerity 3, Fortitude 2, Potence 4, Presence 6 (capped to this system's 1-5 scale above; restore book values at Storyteller discretion for high-power scenes).

system.description: Your skin has become as hard as stone, but loses none of its flexibility. It is now almost impossible to cut you, stake you, or do lasting physical damage to you. Opponents must defeat you in three successive tests to stake you (in addition to winning the necessary Physical Challenge). A character with Flesh of Marble doubles his Health Levels with regard to wounds of a physical nature. Flesh of Marble does not block Disciplines such as Death of the Drum or Cauldron of Blood.

items.name: Presence — 3 Advanced — Form of the Ghost

system.description: While similar to Mist Form in that you become insubstantial, Form of the Ghost allows you to retain your own form and move at a normal pace. Gravity and the elements (except fire and sunlight) do not affect you, effectively giving you a version of flight, and solid objects have no effect on you, allowing you to pass through them at will (though you may not physically manipulate objects in the solid world). You must expend a Blood Trait to enter this form, which may be left at will; the transformation is instantaneous and in some situations may give a Fair Escape. While employing this power you cannot touch or be touched by another character employing this power. You are still affected by wards while in this form, and can utilize any Discipline that does not require touch.

Facetiously named, this power allows the Kindred to physically knock another character away from herself with the slightest of touches. Although this power does no damage in and of itself, its use is quite humbling — to be hurled away from an elder in a social setting has its embarrassing repercussions. Some Kindred use this power surreptitiously, touching their victims and sending them reeling across the room; others use it as a not-so-subtle display of their might, giving their victim a casual slap with overwhelming results.

System: The player spends a Blood Trait and must succeed in a physical challenge to touch the target (this may be done surreptitiously, but the player may not make use of other Potence benefits). The challenge is not required if the subject allows the player to touch him (a handshake, a “friendly” hand on the shoulder, etc). This power hurls the victim 20 feet directly away from the invoking character. If the subject strikes a wall or other solid obstacle, he suffers two health levels of bashing damage. Otherwise, the character needs to win a static physical challenge against six Traits to remain standing.

With this power, the Kindred becomes capable of truly impressive physical displays. He may leap from rooftop to rooftop over entire streets, jump to a fire escape a dozen feet over his head, and perform other feats of athleticism. This is useful both for pursuit and evasion, but is quite a breach of the Masquerade should anyone see this power in use.

System: The player may use this power to allow her character to leap up to 25 feet vertically or 40 feet horizontally. She must succeed in a static physical challenge against four Traits (retest with Athletics) to land correctly — if she fails the challenge, the Storyteller should assess results as appropriate.

Assamites who hone both their preternatural senses and their speed learn a valuable secret: sometimes it is wiser to defend than to attack. A vampire with this power enters a brief trance in which she perceives every threat against her at once, assessing and reacting to each in turn.

System: At the start of a combat turn, before actions are declared, the player spends two Blood Traits and a Willpower Trait to activate this power (this counts as activating Celerity for the turn). The character takes no offensive action that turn, but may defend against every attack made against her, contesting each one individually. This power may be used no more than a number of times per scene equal to the character's Perception Trait total.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two: Saracens
